        <ul class="away">
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>A live demo</strong> — the team brings Sourccey in for teachers and staff before you commit. Request one with the REQUEST DEMO form at the top of this page.</span></li>
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>One training day</strong> at your school, on using the built robot — it lands after Lesson 9, once first power-up is done and driving is next.</span></li>
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>The 163-page Assembly Manual and the full 14-lesson curriculum</strong> — both readable right here on this page.</span></li>
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>Ask Sourccey</strong> — the chat at the bottom of this page, answering from the manual and the curriculum.</span></li>
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>The <a href="https://discord.com/invite/wcxDdcMXhM" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sourccey Discord</a></strong> — the builder community, for the questions the manual doesn&rsquo;t cover.</span></li>
          <li><span class="tick" aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span><strong>Email the sales team</strong> — <a href="mailto:Taylorsalesourccey@gmail.com">Taylorsalesourccey@gmail.com</a>.</span></li>
        </ul>
        <p class="note"><strong>Not published terms:</strong> response times, training beyond the one day above, and a replacement-parts policy are not published anywhere — so they are not promised here. Sourccey is 100% open source, so printed parts can be reprinted from the published files; for anything beyond that, email the team and you&rsquo;ll get a straight answer.</p>

      <!-- OUTCOMES — the concrete list, drawn only from the 14 verified
           lessons. The gallery below is an honest empty state: no
           student names, photos, or projects exist to show yet, and no
           existing film is labeled a trained-policy demo. -->
      <section class="lower-sec lower-outcomes" aria-labelledby="outcomes-h">
        <div class="sec-head">
          <h2 id="outcomes-h"><button class="sec-toggle" id="outcomesToggle" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="outcomesRegion">After 14 lessons, <span class="grad">students can</span> <span class="grad p-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</span></button></h2>
          <div class="rule"></div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-region" id="outcomesRegion"><div class="sec-region-inner">
        <ol class="steps">
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">1</span>
            <div><h4>Build the robot</h4><p>Assemble Sourccey from its printed parts, in the Assembly Manual&rsquo;s build order (Lessons 1&ndash;7).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">2</span>
            <div><h4>Set it up and calibrate it</h4><p>Install the software, run first power-up, and save a calibration (Lessons 8&ndash;9).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">3</span>
            <div><h4>Drive it three ways</h4><p>Teleoperate with the leader arms, the keyboard, and Vulcan Studio (Lesson 10).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">4</span>
            <div><h4>Record clean demonstrations</h4><p>Capture a task — the class example is &ldquo;Fold the shirt&rdquo; — as episodes, keeping only clean takes: at least 5 clean episodes in the class dataset (Lesson 11).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">5</span>
            <div><h4>Train a real AI policy</h4><p>Train on the class&rsquo;s own recorded demonstrations (Lesson 13).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">6</span>
            <div><h4>Roll it out</h4><p>Deploy the trained policy and watch the robot perform the task on its own (Lessons 12 and 14).</p></div>
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="step-n">7</span>
            <div><h4>Present the work</h4><p>Close with the Lesson 14 presentation — what they built, what they taught it, and what they would do differently.</p></div>
          </li>
        </ol>
        <div class="gallery-empty">
          <h3>Student project gallery</h3>
          <p>This gallery is waiting for its first real classroom projects. When classes finish Lesson 14, their robots, datasets, and trained policies will be posted here — real students, real work, nothing staged in the meantime.</p>
          <p>The trained-policy video belongs here too, and it is waiting on the same thing: real classroom footage of a student&rsquo;s own policy running. No existing film is being passed off as one.</p>
        </div>
        </div></div>
      </section>

          <div class="nc-cap-note">Sourccey Approved · School Program</div>
        </div>
      </section>

      <!-- ================= HOW IT WORKS ================= -->
      <section id="nc-how">
        <div class="nc-sec-head">
          <div class="nc-kicker">How This Curriculum Works</div>
          <h2>Four phases, in the manual's build order</h2>
          <p>The 14 lessons run in four phases and follow the Assembly Manual's build order exactly — the class never builds ahead of the manual, and the manual never asks for a part the box has not reached yet. Lessons 1–7 build the robot, Lessons 8–9 bring it to life, Lessons 10–11 drive it and record it, and Lessons 12–14 teach it to perform a task on its own.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="nc-phase-strip">
          <div class="nc-phase-cell" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p1);"><div class="nc-pn">PHASE 1</div><div class="nc-pt">Build It</div><div class="nc-pr">Lessons 1–7</div></div>
          <div class="nc-phase-cell" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p2);"><div class="nc-pn">PHASE 2</div><div class="nc-pt">Bring It to Life</div><div class="nc-pr">Lessons 8–9</div></div>
          <div class="nc-phase-cell" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p3);"><div class="nc-pn">PHASE 3</div><div class="nc-pt">Drive &amp; Record</div><div class="nc-pr">Lessons 10–11</div></div>
          <div class="nc-phase-cell" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p4);"><div class="nc-pn">PHASE 4</div><div class="nc-pt">Teach It</div><div class="nc-pr">Lessons 12–14</div></div>
        </div>

        <h3 style="font-size:17px; margin-top:28px;">Every lesson, the same shape</h3>
        <p style="color:var(--nc-mut); font-size:14.5px; margin-top:6px;">Each lesson lists the same six elements, in the same order:</p>
        <div class="nc-six">
          <div><b>Goal</b><span>The one outcome the lesson exists to produce, stated before anyone picks up a tool.</span></div>
          <div><b>What gets built / done</b><span>The concrete work of the session, in the manual's build order.</span></div>
          <div><b>Session flow</b><span>Open (5 min) — recap and today's goal. Build — the hands-on work. Check — the class verifies the work against the checkoff before anyone packs up.</span></div>
          <div><b>Key skills</b><span>What students are actually practising, so progress can be described to parents and administrators in plain words.</span></div>
          <div><b>Done looks like</b><span>The checkoff: observable, gradeable evidence that the lesson landed. No checkoff, no moving on.</span></div>
          <div><b>Teacher notes</b><span>What to prep before class, and the one stuck point to watch for while students work.</span></div>
        </div>

        <div class="nc-grid2" style="margin-top:26px;">
          <div class="nc-card">
            <h3>The kit teaches the order</h3>
            <p>The kit's trays are packed in build order, so the parts a lesson needs are the parts on top. A team lays out only the current tray zone, builds, and checks off — the box itself enforces the sequence and keeps small parts from wandering.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="nc-card">
            <h3>MAKER classes print ahead</h3>
            <p>In the MAKER edition, each stage's printed parts are printed before the lesson that builds them — the print queue runs one stage ahead of the lessons, so printing never holds a class up. COMPLETE classes skip the queue and start at the tray.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <p style="color:var(--nc-mut); font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.6; margin-top:18px;">One rule runs through all 14 lessons: a stage is finished only when its checkoff passes. A team that finishes early helps another team or practises in the simulator — nobody builds ahead on unverified work.</p>
      </section>

      <!-- ================= PACING ================= -->
      <section id="nc-pacing">
        <div class="nc-sec-head">
          <div class="nc-kicker">Pacing at a Glance</div>
          <h2>One program, two paces</h2>
          <p>The same 14 lessons, run at the pace the school's timetable allows. The phases land in the same order on both lanes — only the weeks change.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="nc-lane">
          <h3>Lane A — 14 Weeks</h3>
          <div class="nc-lane-note">One lesson a week</div>
          <div class="nc-lane-track">
            <div class="nc-seg" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p1); flex:7;"><div class="nc-st">Build It</div><div class="nc-sr">Weeks 1–7 · Lessons 1–7</div></div>
            <div class="nc-seg" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p2); flex:2;"><div class="nc-st">Life</div><div class="nc-sr">Wk 8–9</div></div>
            <div class="nc-seg" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p3); flex:2;"><div class="nc-st">Drive</div><div class="nc-sr">Wk 10–11</div></div>
            <div class="nc-seg" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-p4); flex:3;"><div class="nc-st">Teach It</div><div class="nc-sr">Wks 12–14</div></div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="nc-lane">

          <div class="nc-lane-note">Two lessons a week</div>
